options.why: A full stop shows the end of a sentence.
A question mark shows a question.
Commas separate the things in a list.

hints: Speech marks are also called inverted commas.
Look at a story where the characters talk.
What goes inside the speech marks in a story?
items.explanation: Speech marks go around the exact words that someone says.

items.prompt:
Sam said, “I love kites.”
Which words did Sam say?

options.why: These words tell us who spoke. Sam did not say them.
This is only part of the sentence.
Sam did not say his own name.

hints: Find the speech marks.
The spoken words are inside the speech marks.
Look between the opening “ and the closing ”.
items.explanation: The words inside the speech marks are the words Sam said: I love kites.

items.prompt: Which sentence has the speech marks in the right place?

options.why: Called Joko is not part of what Joko said.
All the spoken words go inside the speech marks.
And play is spoken too, so it belongs inside.

hints: What exact words did Joko say?
Speech marks go around all the spoken words, and only those words.
Check each sentence: are all of Joko's words inside, and nothing else?
items.explanation: Joko said Come and play, so those words go inside the speech marks. Called Joko stays outside.

options.text: “Can I have a drink”? asked Mei.
options.why: The question mark belongs inside the speech marks.

options.text: “Can I have a drink” asked Mei?
options.why: Asked Mei is not a question. The question mark goes after drink.

options.text: “Can I have a drink?” asked Mei.
Can I have a drink? “asked Mei.”
options.why: The speech marks should go around Mei's words.

hints: Mei is asking a question.
The question mark is part of what Mei says.
Look at where each question mark is. Is it inside or outside the speech marks?
items.explanation: The question mark is part of Mei's words, so it goes inside the closing speech mark.

items.prompt:
Write the words that Dewi says, without the speech marks.
“The bus is late,” said Dewi.
hints: Find the speech marks.
Copy only the words inside them.
Stop when you reach the closing speech mark.
items.explanation: Dewi's words are inside the speech marks: The bus is late. The words said Dewi tell us who spoke.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences that are punctuated correctly.

options.why: Shouted Ana should be outside the speech marks.
Said Tom is not spoken, and the full stop is outside.

hints: Check where the speech marks open and close.
Only the spoken words go inside, with their punctuation.
Start with the first sentence. Are only Wayan's words inside?
items.explanation: In the correct sentences, only the spoken words and their punctuation are inside the speech marks.

items.prompt: Put the parts in order to make a sentence with speech.
hints: Find the spoken words first.
The spoken words end with a comma inside the speech marks.
After the spoken words, say who spoke.
items.explanation: The spoken words come first, then said Dad. The comma inside the speech marks shows the sentence carries on.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows the exact words Rina said?

options.text: Rina said that her shoes were wet.
options.why: This tells us what Rina said, but not in her exact words.

options.text: Rina told us about her shoes.
options.why: This does not show her words at all.
This tells us about the shoes, not what Rina said.

hints: Exact words means the words Rina really said.
Exact words go inside speech marks.
Imagine Rina talking. Which sentence sounds like her own voice?
items.explanation: “My shoes are wet,” said Rina shows Rina's exact words in speech marks. Rina said that her shoes were wet tells us about it in other words.

options.text: “We won the match”! shouted the team.
options.why: The exclamation mark is part of what the team said, so it goes inside.

options.text: “We won the match!”, shouted the team.
options.why: The exclamation mark already ends the speech. Do not add a comma after it.

options.text: We won the match! “shouted the team.”
options.why: The speech marks should go around the team's words.

options.text: “We won the match!” shouted the team.

hints: Find the words the team shouted.
The exclamation mark is part of the spoken words.
An exclamation mark already ends the speech. Does it need a comma as well?
items.explanation: The exclamation mark is part of the team's words, so it goes inside the speech marks. No extra comma is needed after it.

items.prompt:
Which word needs a capital letter?
Ben said, “my dog can swim.”

options.why: Said is in the middle of the sentence.
Dog is not a name, and it is not the first spoken word.
Swim is in the middle of what Ben says.

hints: Spoken words start like a new sentence.
Find the first word inside the speech marks.
What does the first word of a sentence always need?
items.explanation: The first spoken word always starts with a capital letter, so my should be My.

items.prompt:
Where should the speech marks go?
Mum asked, Have you fed the fish?

options.text: “Mum asked, Have you fed the fish?”
options.why: Mum asked is not part of what Mum said.

options.text: Mum “asked, Have you fed the fish?”
options.why: Asked is not one of Mum's spoken words.

options.text: Mum asked, “Have you fed the fish?”
Mum asked, “Have you fed” the fish?
options.why: The fish is spoken too, so it belongs inside.

hints: Which words did Mum actually say?
Speech marks open just before the first spoken word.
They close just after the last spoken word and its punctuation.
items.explanation: Mum's words are Have you fed the fish? Those words and the question mark go inside the speech marks.

options.text: “If it rains,” said Kofi, “we can play inside.”
“If it rains,” said Kofi. “we can play inside.”
options.why: The speech carries on, so use a comma after Kofi, not a full stop.

options.text: “If it rains” said Kofi “we can play inside.”
options.why: Commas are needed after rains and after Kofi.

options.text: “If it rains, said Kofi, we can play inside.”
options.why: Said Kofi is not spoken, so it goes outside the speech marks.

hints: Kofi's sentence is split into two parts.
Each part of the speech needs its own speech marks.
Is we can play inside a new sentence, or the rest of the same one?
items.explanation: Kofi's words are split by said Kofi. Each part has speech marks, and we has a small w because the sentence carries on.
